points: in people ≥40 with: persistent or recurrent chest infection; **finger clubbing**; supraclavicular or persistent cervical lymphadenopathy; chest signs consistent with lung cancer; **thrombocytosis**.
**Refer on a suspected cancer pathway** if CXR findings suggest lung cancer, or if aged **≥40 with unexplained haemoptysis**.

**Offer an urgent CXR (within 2 weeks)** to people **≥40** with **two or more** unexplained symptoms — or **one** if they have **ever smoked**: cough, fatigue, shortness of breath, chest pain, weight loss, appetite loss.
Skin metastasis → biopsy (usually via a dermatology urgent pathway) + CT.

items.t: New finger clubbing, haemoptysis, weight loss or persistent cough in a smoker over 40: **urgent CXR / suspected cancer pathway** (NICE NG12).
‘Cellulitis’ on the chest wall after breast cancer that does not respond to antibiotics: think **carcinoma erysipeloides**, urgent referral.

pearls.t: "**Clubbing in a smoker over 40 = chest X-ray.**"
An "**antibiotic-resistant cellulitis**" on the chest wall of a cancer patient may be carcinoma erysipeloides.
